summary: Follow-up of the accepted ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations packet. It retains the 53 R01.5 target IDs by import, separates the trace field, image algebra, trace-dual coordinates, attached Brauer class and Schur index into declarations, and supplies the rank-two group-element Cayley–Hamilton bridge. Existing determinant reconstruction, coefficient descent, Brauer theory and density theory are imported. The remaining nonarchimedean analytic and minuscule/algebraic-monodromy inputs are explicitly bounded gaps; planned coverage does not assert closure.

nodes.title: Trace field of a representation
nodes.statement: Z is the smallest intermediate field of Ω/k containing every matrix trace tr(ρ(g)). It is defined for every n, without absolute irreducibility, finiteness, continuity or a characteristic restriction.
hypotheses: k and Ω are fields with a fixed embedding k → Ω; Γ is a group; ρ:Γ → GL_n(Ω). Write Z=k(tr(ρ(g)):g∈Γ), B=Z[ρ(Γ)].
Full span means Ω·ρ(Γ)=M_n(Ω). For absolutely irreducible ρ over an algebraic closure it is supplied by ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/absolutely-irreducible.
proofSteps: Take the intermediate-field adjoin of the range of the trace function. Its order universal property supplies membership and minimality. Cyclic invariance of trace supplies conjugacy invariance.
acceptance: The statement uses the stated full-span and dimension assumptions; no semisimplicity or splitting hypothesis is silently added.

sources.match: The proof descends a full matrix image algebra using an invertible trace Gram matrix. This packet isolates its algebraic steps; the continuous and rational-eigenvalue conclusions retain their parent IDs.
The trace pairing on an Azumaya algebra is used to descend a generating lattice to the trace ring. Over fields, the same coordinate argument needs no characteristic-zero restriction.
For the absolutely irreducible Cayley–Hamilton quotient the image is central simple of rank d² and has a nondegenerate trace pairing; determinant-law reconstruction itself is imported from IHG.1.

nodes.title: Conjugacy invariance of the trace field
nodes.statement: If ρ′=PρP⁻¹, then traceField(k,ρ)=traceField(k,ρ′) inside Ω.
hypotheses: k and Ω are fields with a fixed embedding k → Ω; Γ is a group; ρ:Γ → GL_n(Ω). Write Z=k(tr(ρ(g)):g∈Γ), B=Z[ρ(Γ)].

proofSteps: Use tr(PMP⁻¹)=tr(M), with the unit inverse identities. The two generating sets of the intermediate-field adjoins are equal.
acceptance: Uses GL-conjugacy rather than entrywise equality; the quaternion test has real traces and nonreal entries.

nodes.title: Image algebra over the trace field
nodes.statement: B is the unital Z-subalgebra of M_n(Ω) generated by the group matrices ρ(g). Its underlying Z-submodule is their linear span. The construction does not assert that B is central simple when the full-span hypothesis fails.
hypotheses: k and Ω are fields with a fixed embedding k → Ω; Γ is a group; ρ:Γ → GL_n(Ω). Write Z=k(tr(ρ(g)):g∈Γ), B=Z[ρ(Γ)].
Full span means Ω·ρ(Γ)=M_n(Ω). For absolutely irreducible ρ over an algebraic closure it is supplied by ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/absolutely-irreducible.
proofSteps: Adjoin the range of the group representation as a subalgebra over Z. Closure under multiplication follows from ρ(g)ρ(h)=ρ(gh), and the identity is ρ(1). The span comparison is promoted as a separate lemma.
acceptance: The statement uses the stated full-span and dimension assumptions; no semisimplicity or splitting hypothesis is silently added.

nodes.title: Image algebra equals the group span
nodes.statement: B.toSubmodule=span_Z(ρ(Γ)), including n=0.
hypotheses: k and Ω are fields with a fixed embedding k → Ω; Γ is a group; ρ:Γ → GL_n(Ω). Write Z=k(tr(ρ(g)):g∈Γ), B=Z[ρ(Γ)].
Full span means Ω·ρ(Γ)=M_n(Ω). For absolutely irreducible ρ over an algebraic closure it is supplied by ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/absolutely-irreducible.
proofSteps: The linear span contains I and is closed under multiplication because products of group generators are group generators. It is therefore a subalgebra containing the generating set. Apply the two minimality properties.
acceptance: A span over the original k is generally too small; the cubic-character test detects it.

nodes.title: A matrix basis from the group image
nodes.statement: Under full span there exist g_i∈Γ and an Ω-basis e_i=ρ(g_i) of M_n(Ω), indexed by Fin(n²).
hypotheses: k and Ω are fields with a fixed embedding k → Ω; Γ is a group; ρ:Γ → GL_n(Ω). Write Z=k(tr(ρ(g)):g∈Γ), B=Z[ρ(Γ)].

proofSteps: Choose a basis inside the spanning range. Its cardinality is n² by the matrix dimension formula; reindex it and choose a preimage g_i of each basis vector.
acceptance: The basis is drawn from group elements, so every Gram entry is a trace of another group element.

nodes.title: Trace-dual descent of coordinates
nodes.statement: If e_i=ρ(g_i) form an Ω-basis of M_n(Ω), then B.toSubmodule=span_Z{e_i}.
hypotheses: k and Ω are fields with a fixed embedding k → Ω; Γ is a group; ρ:Γ → GL_n(Ω). Write Z=k(tr(ρ(g)):g∈Γ), B=Z[ρ(Γ)].
Full span means Ω·ρ(Γ)=M_n(Ω). For absolutely irreducible ρ over an algebraic closure it is supplied by ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/absolutely-irreducible.
proofSteps: Form Q_ij=tr(e_i e_j)=tr(ρ(g_i g_j))∈Z. The matrix trace pairing is nondegenerate by Matrix.ext_iff_trace_mul_right, so Q is invertible over Ω and hence over Z (its determinant lies in Z and is nonzero).
For b∈B, all coordinates of the vector (tr(b e_j)) lie in Z. Solving the Gram system gives the Ω-coordinates of b in Z. This gives the reverse inclusion; basis generators give the forward inclusion.
acceptance: Over characteristic 2 in size 2, tr(I)=0 but tr(E₀₁E₁₀)=1. The pairing remains nondegenerate; no Newton identities or factorial inversions occur.

nodes.title: Canonical scalar extension of the image algebra
nodes.statement: Under full span, the canonical Ω-algebra homomorphism Ω⊗_Z B → M_n(Ω), x⊗b ↦ x·b, is an isomorphism.
hypotheses: k and Ω are fields with a fixed embedding k → Ω; Γ is a group; ρ:Γ → GL_n(Ω). Write Z=k(tr(ρ(g)):g∈Γ), B=Z[ρ(Γ)].
Full span means Ω·ρ(Γ)=M_n(Ω). For absolutely irreducible ρ over an algebraic closure it is supplied by ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1/absolutely-irreducible.
proofSteps: Use the tensor universal property to define multiplication on pure tensors. It is onto because every matrix is an Ω-linear combination of the e_i. Both sides have Ω-dimension n², so the map is bijective; bundle its algebra equivalence.
acceptance: The equivalence is fixed on pure tensors, so it is the canonical map rather than an unspecified abstract isomorphism.

nodes.title: Faithful determinant quotient of the image algebra
nodes.statement: For n>0 and full span, let φ:Z[Γ]→B be the Z-algebra map sending [g] to ρ(g). It is onto. For x∈Z[Γ], φ(x)=0 iff charpoly(bφ(x))=X^n for every b∈B. Under the determinant-law kernel convention of IHG.1, this detects exactly ker(D), where D is det∘φ, and hence identifies Z[Γ]/ker(D) with B.
hypotheses: k and Ω are fields with a fixed embedding k → Ω; Γ is a group; ρ:Γ → GL_n(Ω). Write Z=k(tr(ρ(g)):g∈Γ), B=Z[ρ(Γ)].

proofSteps: Form the Ω-valued matrix determinant law using IHG.0/determinant-of-matrix-representation. All group characteristic coefficients lie in Z, so IHG.0/determinant-coefficient-subring descends it to the coefficient subring and then extends it to Z. This constructs the determinant D rather than assuming a pointwise determinant function is a polynomial law.

Surjectivity follows from the Z-span of the group matrices. A zero matrix has characteristic polynomial X^n after any left multiplication. Conversely the coefficient of X^(n−1) gives tr(bφ(x))=0 for all b; full Ω-span and the nondegenerate trace pairing force φ(x)=0.

The universal determinant-law kernel is contained in these tests over B and therefore in ker(φ). The other inclusion holds after every scalar extension because φ(x)=0 persists. The first isomorphism theorem gives the quotient comparison. The suggested declaration exposes the surjectivity and concrete matrix-kernel test; the abstract determinant and its quotient use the existing IHG interfaces.
acceptance: Testing only det(φ(x))=0 would describe singular matrices and is not a kernel; all left-multiplication tests are essential.

nodes.title: Polarization of rank-two group-element relations
nodes.statement: There is an F-linear involutive anti-automorphism s of F[Γ], s([g])=det(r([g]))[g⁻¹]. For every x, x+s(x)−tr(r(x))·1∈J and x·s(x)−det(r(x))·1∈J. This one declaration collects the relations proved simultaneously in BLR Proposition 1.
hypotheses: F is an arbitrary field, Γ a group, and r:F[Γ]→M₂(F) a unital F-algebra homomorphism.
For each g, r([g]) is invertible. J is the two-sided ideal generated by [g]²−tr(r([g]))[g]+det(r([g]))·1 for every g∈Γ.
proofSteps: The determinant character defines the anti-involution on the group basis and extends F-linearly. On 2×2 matrices it is the adjugate, a linear map satisfying adj(AB)=adj(B)adj(A).

The relation for one group element gives x+s(x)≡tr(r(x)) on the basis and hence on every x. Apply it to the relevant group products and polarize to obtain the determinant relation for finite linear combinations. Follow the characteristic-free calculation of Proposition 1.
acceptance: Works in characteristic 2. It extends relations from group elements, rather than assuming relations for every element of the group algebra.

nodes.title: Kernel of a full rank-two image
nodes.statement: If r:F[Γ]→M₂(F) is surjective, then J=ker(r) as two-sided ideals.
hypotheses: F is an arbitrary field, Γ a group, and r:F[Γ]→M₂(F) a unital F-algebra homomorphism.
For each g, r([g]) is invertible. J is the two-sided ideal generated by [g]²−tr(r([g]))[g]+det(r([g]))·1 for every g∈Γ.
r is surjective.
proofSteps: Cayley–Hamilton gives J⊂ker(r). Work in F[Γ]/J with its induced onto matrix map. For x in its kernel, the polarized relations imply yx=xy* and show that the annihilator of x is a two-sided ideal whose matrix image contains matrix commutators.

Since M₂(F) is noncommutative and simple, that image ideal is all matrices. Choose w annihilating x whose matrix image is I. The determinant relation gives w·w*=1, so w is invertible in the quotient and x=0. This proves the opposite kernel inclusion.
acceptance: Surjectivity is the full-span/Burnside output; a reducible or scalar rank-two image is excluded. No characteristic restriction on F is used.

nodes.title: Rank-two annihilation implies isotypy
nodes.statement: Let r:F[Γ]→M₂(F) be onto and let σ:Γ→GL_N(F), with N finite. If charpoly(r([g])) evaluated on σ(g) vanishes for every g∈Γ, then there exist m≥0 and a Γ-equivariant F-linear isomorphism F^N≃F²⊗_F F^m, where Γ acts through r on F² and trivially on the multiplicity space. Thus N=2m and σ is semisimple and isotypic.
hypotheses: F is an arbitrary field, Γ a group, and r:F[Γ]→M₂(F) a unital F-algebra homomorphism.
For each g, r([g]) is invertible. J is the two-sided ideal generated by [g]²−tr(r([g]))[g]+det(r([g]))·1 for every g∈Γ.
r is onto; σ has finite dimension N (N=0 is permitted).
proofSteps: Extend σ to F[Γ]. The annihilation hypothesis kills each generator of J, hence kills ker(r) by the preceding kernel theorem. The module therefore factors through M₂(F).

The full matrix action kills CH(det r), including all polarized relations: apply matrix Cayley–Hamilton after adjoining formal scalar variables, not only to group matrices. This verifies the imported module-recognition hypothesis.

Apply the imported full matrix-module equivalence: the multiplicity space is E₁₁F^N and the module is F²⊗E₁₁F^N. Choose a basis of that finite-dimensional space to obtain F^m; the matrix action gives equivariance.
acceptance: For N=0 take m=0. For a standard rank-two representation, take m=1. A nonsplit extension satisfying these relations cannot survive.

The theorem is rank-two-specific. BLR §5, pp.327–328 gives a rank-three A₄ example where elementwise annihilation does not force isotypy; this is not replaced by an unrestricted-degree Cayley–Hamilton assertion.

gaps.title: Nonarchimedean analytic Haar-null bridge
gaps.detail: For a compact open subgroup G of H(E), E a finite extension of ℚ_ℓ and H a smooth closed algebraic subgroup of GL_n, construct nonarchimedean analytic charts and identify Haar measure locally with a nonvanishing analytic density times additive chart measure. gaps.detail: Nek18 Proposition 3.10 is now read with its actual hypotheses: (A′) each W_i is a sum of simple modules for the ℚ̄_ℓ-span of Lie(ρ_i(Γ)), each simple module one-dimensional or minuscule; (C′) an open Γ′, a dense Σ and a positive integer a satisfy P_(⊗ρ_i)(g^a)(σ(g^a))=0 for g∈Σ. Case (3) requires a=r=1 and W_1 minuscule. Its conclusion is global semisimplicity of σ and σ|Γ′≅ρ_1|Γ′^⊕m, not automatically global isotypy for an arbitrary Γ. Needed declarations: the finite-local-coefficient/logarithm passage for compact profinite images; minuscule weight detection under semisimplification of a module with unipotent radical (Theorem 3.7, Proposition 1.3(2) and §§1.4–1.5); verification for the standard sp₄/gsp₄ module; and the finite-component argument turning the open-subgroup result into the retained GSp₄ target. The rank-two BLR input is separately supplied and must not be used as a theorem in arbitrary rank.

gaps.title: Induced GSp₄ and Asai algebraic-monodromy inputs
gaps.detail: BCGP25V1 Proposition 4.11.2, pp.110–112, still needs algebraic Goursat with quotient representability; the char-zero normal-unipotent/radical argument; classification up to central twist of simple representations of the relevant quotient of SL₂×SL₂; verification that the twisted Asai image has closures O₄ and SO₄; and the classification of closed subgroups of N⋊O₄ surjecting onto O₄, with the degree-five minimal-polynomial witness in the nonsplit case. The last two are representation-specific R01.5/G7 inputs. ReductiveGroups layers 3, 5 and 6 supply the surrounding notions, but their current contracts do not explicitly export algebraic Goursat or the specialized SL₂×SL₂ classification. These additions need a Part II with exact targets. The Ext¹ restriction/induction comparison used here must be owned in this lower-tier direction and imported by ArithmeticGaloisDuality, rather than introducing an upward prerequisite.

imports.rule: Retain these 53 IDs and their declarations. New carrier and comparison IDs refine their proof dependencies; they do not replace the principal target IDs or edit the parent packet.

principalRefinement.assembly: Keep the principal parent ID as the descent-obstruction target. Replace its bundled trace-field/image-algebra/trace-coordinate/central-simple/Brauer/index clauses by the named declarations here. Reconcile the parent’s prototype names with these actual baseline Brauer constructors and equal trace-field transports.

prerequisiteRefinements.contract: Use algebraically closed reconstruction in every characteristic and the arbitrary-field faithful quotient, retaining the imperfect-field finiteness qualifications; an arbitrary determinant is not assumed to come from a k-valued representation.

Henselian Cayley–Hamilton reconstruction requires the residual determinant to be absolutely irreducible AND split. Coefficient descent uses the complete Noetherian subring contract with the same residue field and a strict conjugator; it is already owned upstream.

Distinguish GSp recognition with two given perfect alternating forms from descent of a form. The imported coefficient-descent result assumes p>2 and the full multiplier valued in the subring. It supplies no characteristic-two descent theorem.

The BLR input is now a named theorem. Invoke it only after obtaining the full rank-two image and extending dense Frobenius annihilation to every group element. The higher-rank monodromy and extension arguments remain explicit gaps.

The baseline supplies this instance under the nonisolated-identity, T1, weak local compactness and Borel hypotheses. Use its additive counterpart for E^d. It does not supply nonarchimedean analytic charts or their Haar measure comparison.

upstreamNotes.note: Current layer 4 is read directly: it does not state a generic reduced characteristic polynomial/reduced trace API. The parent remaining list treated it as a supplier. This packet supplies only the attached matrix coefficient descent via separable splitting. Generic reduced characteristic polynomials and their scalar-extension/reduced-norm API belong in Semisimple algebras, Part II.

Current layers 3, 5 and 6 cover quotients, unipotent radicals and char-zero reductivity but do not explicitly state algebraic Goursat or the specialized SL₂×SL₂ quotient representation classification. Record exact extensions rather than claiming those named theorems are existing targets.
